summary: The virtio network driver on QEMU's virtio-net-pci in each form the device takes, each case a boot of its own that tests/cases/machine/virtionet_scenario.c drives

cases.behavior: a virtio network device as QEMU makes it becomes eth0 with a vector for each queue, mergeable receive buffers, the event index and the control queue; vnetprobe reads its link files, pings the gateway, lets the driver go, which takes the interface away, binds it again through /sys, which makes a new one, configures that and pings again; and the cable pulled out and put back through QMP is logged at each, with a ping answered after

steps.does: boot the test image to the debug shell
read the boot log for the driver's lines
run vnetprobe at the debug shell and take its report from the console
pull the card's cable out and put it back with QMP's set_link, waiting for the driver's line at each, then ping the gateway from the debug shell

assertions.checks: the boot log has the virtio device as the first interface, `net: eth0: virtio_net`
the device has a vector for each of its three queues, `virtio: interrupts: virtio0: msi-x`
the driver's line names mergeable buffers, the event index and the control queue after its 128 receive and 64 transmit buffers
the interface's carrier reads 1, and its speed, duplex and mtu read what the device says: -1, unknown and 1500 for a device that gives none, as Linux's files read
the network device of /sys/bus/virtio/devices has a driver link whose last name is virtio_net, and the interface's device link leads to that device below its PCI function, as Linux's does
a ping to the gateway gets a reply
the function's name written to /sys/bus/pci/drivers/virtio-pci/unbind takes the device off the virtio bus
the interface goes with the device, as Linux's virtnet_remove unregisters it: /sys/class/net has it no more, SIOCGIFINDEX of its name fails with ENODEV, and a ping to the gateway fails

the function's name written to /sys/bus/pci/drivers/virtio-pci/bind brings the device back with its driver link and a new interface of the same name, the lowest free, with an ifindex that is not the old one's, down, as Linux leaves a new interface, whose device link leads to the device
the new interface set up, given 10.0.2.15/24 and a default route through the gateway with SIOCSIFFLAGS, SIOCSIFADDR, SIOCSIFNETMASK and SIOCADDRT reads a carrier of 1
a ping to the gateway gets a reply over the device bound again
the driver logs `virtio_net: link: virtio0: down` once the cable is out
the driver logs `virtio_net: link: virtio0: up` once the cable is back
the debug shell's ping of the gateway gets a reply after the cable is back

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: it tests the driver of QEMU's virtio network device, which the Lenovo does not have; the Lenovo's own card is checked by the release's metal_accept.sh

cases.behavior: a virtio network card put in slot 6 of a machine booted without one, through QMP's device_add, is announced by the firmware's GPE method with a Notify of the slot, as Linux's acpiphp takes it: the kernel lists the function, gives its BARs addresses in the host bridge's windows and binds it as eth0; vnetprobe sets up the new interface and passes its rows; QMP's device_del has the kernel let go of the card and run the slot's _EJ0, after which QEMU has nothing in the slot, and the card put in again comes up again

steps.does: boot the test image, with no network card, to the debug shell
read the boot log for the hot plug slots

add a user network with QMP's netdev_add, run vnetprobe plugged=1 at the debug shell, put a virtio-net-pci card on that network in slot 6 with QMP's device_add once it asks and wait for the kernel to list and bind it, take the card out with QMP's device_del once it asks, wait for the kernel to eject it and read QEMU's query-pci, put the card in again once it asks, and take the probe's report from the console

assertions.checks: the boot log has the host bridge's 30 hot plug slots on bus 0 taken, every slot but the host bridge's and the PIIX's, `pci: hotplug: 30 slots on bus 0`
after QMP's device_add of a virtio-net-pci card in slot 6 the kernel logs the function added, `pci: hotplug: added: 00:06.0 1af4:`, and the driver binds it as eth0, `virtio_net: bound: virtio0: eth0`
the hot plugged card's interface is down, as Linux leaves a new interface, and is set up, given 10.0.2.15/24 and a default route through the gateway, after which its carrier reads 1
the interface's carrier reads 1, and its speed, duplex and mtu read what the device says: -1, unknown and 1500 for a device that gives none, as Linux's files read
the network device of /sys/bus/virtio/devices has a driver link whose last name is virtio_net, and the interface's device link leads to that device below its PCI function, as Linux's does
a ping to the gateway gets a reply

the interface goes with the device, as Linux's virtnet_remove unregisters it: /sys/class/net has it no more, SIOCGIFINDEX of its name fails with ENODEV, and a ping to the gateway fails

the function's name written to /sys/bus/pci/drivers/virtio-pci/bind brings the device back with its driver link and a new interface of the same name, the lowest free, with an ifindex that is not the old one's, down, as Linux leaves a new interface, whose device link leads to the device
the new interface set up, given 10.0.2.15/24 and a default route through the gateway with SIOCSIFFLAGS, SIOCSIFADDR, SIOCSIFNETMASK and SIOCADDRT reads a carrier of 1
a ping to the gateway gets a reply over the device bound again
after the card is taken out, the interface is gone from /sys/class/net and SIOCGIFINDEX of its name fails with ENODEV
the interface of the card put in again is down, is set up, and gets a reply to a ping to the gateway

after QMP's device_del the driver logs the interface removed, `virtio_net: removed: virtio0: eth0`, the kernel logs the slot ejected after its _EJ0, `pci: hotplug: ejected: slot 6`, and QEMU's query-pci then has no device in slot 6
the card put in slot 6 again with QMP's device_add is listed and bound as eth0 again
